newsitem.title: USA: U.S. economy on growth, low inflation path - Yellen.
newsitem.headline: U.S. economy on growth, low inflation path - Yellen.

text.p: White House economic advisor Janet Yellen said on Friday that the U.S. economy was on track for sustained growth and low inflation.
"All the available evidence suggests that our economy is on a sustainable trajectory for continued job creation and solid growth and output," she said at a White House news briefing.
"The main symptom of economic overheating, if it were occurring, would be rising inflation, and we simply have not seen that," she said.
Yellen said that, with a falling deficit, low and stable inflation, lean inventories, and strong growth, "this expansion remains on a very solid footing."
She said revised Q1 GDP figures released Friday, which showed the economy growing at an annualized 5.8 percent rate, confirmed the economy was enjoying a remarkable period.
She said she expected a moderation in later quarters in some indicators.

"My expectation is that consumption spending will moderate as we go forward toward a somewhat lower pace than we saw in the first quarter. The first quarter ... was really very exceptional," she said.

"I don't see any of the likely factors," Yellen said of things that could bring the current economic expansion to an end, mentioning rising inflation and inventory overhangs as things she would look for.
She said the economy had outperformed almost everthing the White House had assumed in putting together its budget plan.
"To meet our real growth forecast for this year, in fact, we would meet it even if there was no further economic growth over the next three quarters."
